1: The first MLB game in the archive turned into an 11-inning, 1–0 Dodger Stadium classic—and a remarkably dense time capsule. Four future Hall of Famers shared the field: [[134181|Adrian Beltré]], [[115749|Rickey Henderson]], [[123833|Larry Walker]] and [[115732|Todd Helton]].

For 10 innings, neither side could break through. [[111554|Kevin Brown]] gave Los Angeles eight scoreless innings, allowing three hits with six strikeouts, while Colorado starter [[276336|Shawn Chacon]] matched him with seven scoreless frames and six strikeouts. [[150378|Eric Gagne]] struck out three in a clean ninth to keep the game even.

The Dodgers finally finished it in the 11th. [[133321|Alex Cora]] singled and scored the only run when [[115094|Shawn Green]] lined a walk-off single to center. Green went 2-for-5 with the RBI, sending the archive’s first MLB night home on a one-run walk-off.
2: Cincinnati and Los Angeles traded first-inning runs, with [[115135|Ken Griffey Jr.]] bringing home Ryan Freel on a sacrifice fly before César Izturis answered with a solo homer. The tie did not last long.

[[150178|Jason LaRue]] delivered the decisive swing in the second, a three-run homer that put the Reds ahead for good. He added a two-run shot in the ninth, finishing 2-for-3 with two home runs, five RBI and two runs scored in a 6–1 Cincinnati win.

[[407799|Brandon Claussen]] handled the rest from the mound, holding the Dodgers to one run on four hits across seven innings with five strikeouts. [[434885|D.J. Houlton]] struck out four over six innings for Los Angeles, but the two LaRue homers supplied nearly all the separation Cincinnati needed.
3: Los Angeles and Toronto played an 11-inning back-and-forth at Angel Stadium. The Angels opened the scoring in the second when [[115223|Vladimir Guerrero]] came home on an error, but the Blue Jays answered in the fifth on [[407861|Orlando Hudson]]’s RBI double before [[408210|Chone Figgins]] put Los Angeles back in front later that inning.

The lead changed again in a three-run Toronto seventh. Hudson’s second RBI of the night started the surge, and the Blue Jays went ahead 4–3. Figgins’ eighth-inning forceout brought home [[430895|Maicer Izturis]] to tie it, setting up extra innings after the bullpens kept the score level.

In the 11th, [[111851|Orlando Cabrera]] singled and came around on [[113889|Darin Erstad]]’s walk-off single to left. [[150456|Adam Kennedy]] supplied a 4-for-5 night with an RBI, while [[276912|Scot Shields]] worked two scoreless innings to earn the win in the 5–4 Angels finish.
4: The Dodgers did all their scoring in the first inning against San Diego, capitalizing on a Mark Loretta error before [[425854|Oscar Robles]] drove a double into right. [[430632|Willy Aybar]] and [[400292|Hee-Seop Choi]] both scored on the play, giving Los Angeles a three-run cushion before the game settled into a pitching duel.

[[117955|Derek Lowe]] made the early lead stand. He limited the Padres to one run across 7.2 innings, scattering seven hits with four strikeouts. San Diego finally got on the board in the eighth, when [[137001|Robert Fick]] singled home [[150353|Dave Roberts]], but could not produce another breakthrough.

[[400093|Duaner Sánchez]] entered to get the final four outs and earned the save, preserving a 3–1 Dodgers win. The game’s only two scoring plays came seven innings apart, with Lowe’s start giving Los Angeles exactly the room it needed.
5: A 13-inning game at Angel Stadium featured three future Hall of Famers—[[400085|Ichiro Suzuki]], [[134181|Adrian Beltré]] and [[115223|Vladimir Guerrero]]—and an early Angels lead that would not hold. Guerrero opened the scoring with a second-inning homer, then came around again during Los Angeles’ three-run third, capped by [[121640|Tim Salmon]]’s two-run single.

Seattle fought back from a 4–1 deficit. [[435358|Yuniesky Betancourt]] homered in the third, Beltré reached on an error that scored Carl Everett in the fourth, and [[430598|Jeremy Reed]] tied it with a solo homer in the fifth. The score stayed 4–4 for seven full innings as both bullpens absorbed the extra-inning workload.

[[122027|Richie Sexson]] finally broke through in the 13th with a solo homer to center. [[430941|George Sherrill]] delivered two scoreless innings for the win, and [[430646|Jake Woods]] finished the 5–4 Seattle victory with a scoreless 13th for the save.
6: Atlanta and New York played a 12-inning game that swung twice after the eighth. [[116662|Andruw Jones]] put the Braves ahead in the fourth with a double that scored [[121074|Edgar Renteria]], and [[435263|Brian McCann]] made it 2–0 in the sixth with an RBI single after [[116706|Chipper Jones]] reached home.

The Yankees chipped away. [[121347|Alex Rodriguez]] grounded out to score Melky Cabrera in the sixth, then [[114739|Jason Giambi]]’s eighth-inning solo homer forced extra innings. [[122477|John Smoltz]] gave Atlanta seven innings of one-run ball with five strikeouts, while [[425426|Chien-Ming Wang]] matched him with eight innings and two earned runs allowed.

[[279578|Marcus Giles]] briefly put Atlanta back in front with a 12th-inning homer, but New York had the final answer. Kevin Reese reached, and Rodriguez ended it with a two-run walk-off homer to left off [[407901|Jorge Sosa]], giving the Yankees a 4–3 finish.
